assumptions: Assumption: Canonical EV surface markers (or phosphatidylserine capture ligands) are present and detectable on MSC-derived small EVs from the chosen source cells.
Assumption: Particle enumeration methods (NTA, TRPS, or similar) correlate sufficiently with EV-associated marker signal to allow discrimination.
Assumption: Detergent and protease/RNase treatments reliably differentiate membrane-protected from soluble signals under the assay conditions.
biological_rationale: EVs are membranous particles that protect surface and luminal components from external protease/RNase unless membrane integrity is disrupted; correlating particle counts with membrane-protected marker signal distinguishes particle-associated material from freely soluble non-vesicular cargo. (Inference: uses canonical EV biology; supported by MISEV2023 recommendation for orthogonal characterization.)

candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity (intact-EV signature)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: An intact-EV-associated signature (capture of surface markers that is particle-correlated and detergent/protease-sensitive) is needed to discriminate an EV-enriched drug substance from a secretome that contains non‑vesicular co-isolates; aligns with MISEV2023 recommendations.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: marker choice and assay sensitivity may vary by source cell and isolation method; this attribute is exploratory until validated with program-specific materials.

edges.competing_explanation: Marker enrichment could reflect co‑isolation of protein aggregates or lipoproteins that co-sediment with particles.
edges.missing_experiment: Program-specific intact-EV capture and protection studies with matched purified and unpurified preparations.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal approaches but does not define a single discriminating panel for all source-cell types.

edges.competing_explanation: A true EV-enriched preparation might still fail in biodistribution if dosing or route-specific barriers exist.
edges.missing_experiment: Matched intact-EV analytics in large-animal dosing studies.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: lack of CNS detection after intranasal dosing may arise from formulation, administration, or labeling choices rather than absence of intact EVs.

edges.competing_explanation: Even with a defined identity attribute, potency linkage may remain unresolved if active cargo is not EV-associated.
edges.missing_experiment: Potency assays specifically linked to the intact-EV-associated signature.
edges.uncertainty: Inference: Translational and manufacturing recommendations follow from knowing fractionation state; uncertainty remains about how identity maps to potency in this program.

nodes.statement: The product is currently defined as 'secretome retaining EVs' versus a purified small‑EV drug substance; this distinction is unresolved and blocks product definition and CMC decisions.

If a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (intact-EV capture, particle counts, detergent/protease sensitivity, density correlation) is observed, then the preparation can be classified as an EV-enriched small‑EV preparation rather than mainly non‑vesicular secretome.

If no membrane-protected, particle-associated signature is observed and marker signal tracks with bulk soluble protein and is insensitive to membrane disruption, then the preparation is indistinguishable from an unpurified secretome with co-isolated non‑vesicular components.
Classifying the drug‑substance fractionation state enables targeted CMC actions: orthogonal QC panel, potency assay development, and relevant scale-up comparability testing (MISEV2023 guidance).

competing_explanations: Co‑isolated non-vesicular particles (protein aggregates, lipoproteins) could give particle counts and marker-like signals, generating false classification.
Source-cell, isolation method, or formulation components may mask or strip markers, reducing sensitivity of the intact-EV signature.
dependencies: Define source-cell lot and processing SOPs for matched conditioned medium preparations (links to manufacturing actions: source-cell bank and representative scale-up).
Access to orthogonal characterization resources and capture reagents.
design_question: Which measurable composition distinction can discriminate a secretome-retaining-EV product from a small-EV preparation?
expected_measurable_effect: Enrichment of membrane-protected EV surface markers (e.g., CD63/CD9/CD81 or phosphatidylserine capture) that co-localize with particle-count peaks and density fractions consistent with small EVs, with signal loss after detergent (Triton X-100) and protection from external protease/RNase unless membrane-disrupted.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow combining: (1) density-gradient fractionation followed by particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection of EV surface markers on intact material per fraction; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched preparations: (A) enriched small-EV preparation vs (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining EVs) from the same source-cell lot.
experiment.control: Negative control: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples; Positive control: commercially available characterized small EVs if available.
dependencies: Availability of consistent source-cell conditioned medium lots (same passage/bank)
Access to validated capture reagents and particle counting instrumentation
experiment.failure_criterion: No qualitative difference between enriched small-EV preparation and secretome control in co-localization of capture signal with particle peaks, or lack of membrane-protection behavior (i.e., captured signal unaffected by detergent/protease/RNase) indicating inability to discriminate fractionation state.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If the criteria for success are not met across independent replicates, the hypothesis is falsified and the program must treat the material as indistinguishable from secretome with respect to intact-EV identity and re-evaluate fractionation strategy.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (immuno-capture of EV surface markers + particle enumeration + detergent/protease protection + density fractionation) will be observed in a purified small-EV preparation but not in an unpurified concentrated secretome.
experiment.primary_readout: Co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment (indicating membrane protection).
experiment.question: Can an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature discriminate an EV-enriched small-EV preparation from an unpurified MSC secretome?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed as: (A) small-EV enrichment (e.g., ultracentrifugation/SEC) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium without EV enrichment
Purified small-EV positive control from orthogonal source (if available)
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Protease (e.g., proteinase K) and RNase reagents
Detergent (e.g., Triton X-100) for membrane disruption
secondary_readouts: Presence/absence of marker signal in secretome control fractions
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned medium preps)
experiment.success_criterion: Observed enrichment of capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-count peaks in density fractions for the small-EV enriched preparation, and a significant reduction (> qualitative loss) of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase, while the unpurified secretome shows marker signal that does not co-localize with particle peaks and is largely insensitive to membrane-disrupting treatments (qualitative comparison).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Membrane protection assays (protease/RNase sensitivity with and without detergent) combined with immuno-capture and particle enumeration provide a testable, orthogonal signature that discriminates particle-associated EV signal from soluble non-vesicular components (based on MISEV2023 principles).
falsification_criteria: Falsified if preparations that meet the intact-EV signature (capture-positive, particle-correlated, detergent/protease-sensitive) consistently fail to show enrichment of particle-associated markers versus concentrated conditioned medium, i.e., no measurable discrimination.

Falsified if detergent and protease/RNase treatments do not differentially affect captured signal between purified small-EV preparations and unpurified secretome controls (no membrane-protection observed).
human_decisions_required: Select canonical EV surface markers or capture strategy appropriate for MSC-derived EVs (CD63/CD9/CD81 vs TIM4/AnxA5).
Approve experimental resources and accept qualitative success/failure criteria for this stage.
Decide on follow-up potency linkage experiments if discrimination is successful.
manufacturability_assessment: Establishing this attribute is manufacturable at analytical scale (requires capture reagents, validated particle counters, density fractionation capability) and would inform selection of a drug-substance fractionation process; however, implementation requires development resources and assay validation.
manufacturing_rationale: An analytically discriminating identity attribute is required to define drug-substance fractionation state (secretome retaining EVs vs enriched small-EV isolate) and to enable downstream release, comparability, and potency linkage activities as recommended by consensus guidance.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal panel: (1) particle enumeration by NTA/TRPS of input and density fractions; (2) immuno-capture ELISA (capture for CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 phosphatidylserine capture) for surface markers on intact material; (3) protease and RNase protection assays +/- detergent to assess membrane protection of captured signal; (4) density-gradient correlation (fractionation) to align marker and particle peaks; (5) total protein and protein:particle ratio assessment to detect non‑vesicular protein load. Include matched controls: purified small-EV isolate (positive control), concentrated conditioned medium without EV enrichment (negative control), and detergent-disrupted samples.
principal_risks: False-positive classification due to co-isolated non-vesicular particles that mimic particle-associated signatures.
Insufficient sensitivity of capture reagents or particle counting to detect relevant EV populations from the chosen source-cell/process.
Resource and timeline impact from assay development and validation requirements.
proposed_potency_relationship: If biological activity in downstream potency assays co-varies with the intact-EV-associated signature across preparations and fractionation states, this supports a potency relationship to EV-associated cargo; otherwise, activity may be driven by soluble, non‑vesicular components.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Define an orthogonal intact-EV-associated signature (immuno-capture of canonical EV surface markers + particle enumeration + detergent/protease protection and density-fraction correlation) as a discriminating product-identity attribute between a small-EV preparation and an unpurified secretome.
title: Hypothesis: A membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature will discriminate an EV-enriched small‑EV preparation from an unpurified MSC secretome that retains non‑vesicular co‑isolates
